system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft vs Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Several positions would reach our protections in ways the Seller's cover note doesn't flag, including the title override, the fraud carve-out gap, the blanket disclosure and knowledge exclusions, and the post-Completion Riverlark release. We should not treat any of it as settled.

## 1. "FINAL" and "settled at principal level"

The cover note says the positions were settled by both deal teams and are "not intended to be re-opened." We have no record of that. Under the playbook, the only concession we can make on the cap (20%/AUD 4.8m) or the claims period (18 months) requires written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given. The Seller's "market context" ranges (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods) are the Seller's framing, not our standard, and they sit below our own starting positions. Our response should say so directly and should not accept any of these as a baseline.

## 2. Departure matrix

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% only with Frost authority | Reject; reopen at 25% |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded (tipping) | Reject; deductible structure is a major departure |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 only with Frost approval | Reject |
| Cross-application of limits (12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims | No hidden general-regime override | Reject; this is the dangerous clause |
| Title / capacity (Fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge | Reject outright |
| Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these, non-waivable | Reject; add fraud carve-out |
| General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2; Sch 7) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket exclusion incl. data room and public records | Delete; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject |
| Bluefen (3/6.3; DL §2) | Reasonable endeavours; consent satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion | Reject; no final consent exists |
| Riverlark (2/7; DL §3) | ~AUD 3.2m released post-Completion | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases | Reject |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL §5) | AUD 420k excluded; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded; not silently excluded | Reject; on-costs also unaddressed |
| Ironquay IP (11.1; DL §4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure | Reject; AUD 180k unverified |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6/Sch 6; DL §6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; no assumed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum | Neither accept nor reject the characterisation; require evidence |
| Sandbar renewals (DL §8) | "Ordinary-course" | Assess; no automatic debt or price deduction | Assess; reject characterisation until evidenced |
| Tax / IP (cover note) | "Settled under the general regime" | Separate categories; terms open; no unlimited liability assumed | Reject folding into general regime |
| Title (cover note; DL §10) | DD-012 register evidences 100% title | DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Reject as sufficient |

## 3. Key issues and reasoning

**a. Title override (most serious).** Putting title and capacity under the general cap, time limit and basket means a title defect could be capped at AUD 4.8m, expire at 18 months, and sit behind a AUD 250k deductible. Title needs its own regime. The Seller's support for title is the DD-012 register, which is a supplied source and does not establish independent ownership, encumbrances or authority. We should require ASIC extracts, PPSR and encumbrance searches, share transfer and authority documents, and evidence of board and shareholder approvals.

**b. Fraud carve-out.** The Seller's limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language covers "all Claims of any nature." Without an express carve-out, an exclusive-remedy clause could be argued to bar a fraud claim. Our playbook requires the carve-out to the maximum extent enforceable and says no one may waive it. This must be explicit in the draft.

**c. Disclosure and knowledge.** Combined, the whole-data-room disclosure (1.1) and the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (8.3) could defeat most warranty claims. Anything in DD-002 to DD-012 would be disclosed, and anything discoverable from the data room would be excluded. Together these operate as a general release. We should require specific fair disclosure and delete 8.3.

**d. Bluefen.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The DL confirms no final written consent and no evidence the conditions in clause 11.3 are met. "Consent satisfied on delivery" is not acceptable. Consent and condition evidence must be in hand before Completion, and reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a material customer consent.

**e. Riverlark.** The facility has about AUD 3.2m outstanding and has not been repaid (DL §3). A post-Completion release leaves security in place after we have paid the price. We need a current payoff letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**f. Funds flow and bonuses.** The DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k) are conditional on Completion and continued employment, but they are missing from the funds flow. Payroll tax and superannuation are unaddressed (DL §5). These must be a specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs. Otherwise, we would inherit the liability at Completion without the price adjustment.

**g. Ironquay.** Clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of the SOW3 project materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180k open figure (DD-010) is not independent verification of non-payment either way. The indemnity should cover the IP transfer and title to the project materials and the cost of any cure, not only the SOW3 payment. We should ask for proof of payment or a confirmatory assignment. We should not assume the AUD 180k is right or wrong.

**h. Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** The DL says the material does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required. The export may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. The Seller calls this "not expected to be material." We should not adopt that view or assume a breach either way. Our asks are log preservation, a completed investigation with a timetable, and regular written updates. Privacy counsel should assess the notification question under the Privacy Act and the NDB scheme. We should also consider whether a specific indemnity or other protection is appropriate. That is a judgment for the deal team, not a playbook requirement.

**i. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. DL §8 says the material does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should assess them and request the contracts and terms. Under the playbook we should not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct from price.

**j. Tax and IP.** The Seller wants these folded into the general regime. Under our playbook they remain open categories, and we should not assume unlimited liability or treat them as resolved. Each needs its own regime and its own negotiation.

**k. Items not addressed by the playbook.** Mossvale (DL §9) and the office lease (DL §7) both have restrictions or notice obligations, but the DL does not say whether consent is required for the share sale. We need counsel to confirm whether a change of control triggers either provision. Separately, the DL states its facts as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. We should require a bring-down of all disclosures and an updated data room before signing and Completion.

## 4. Recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled" position.** Respond that no principal-level agreement has been recorded and that our positions are unchanged. Any movement toward 20% or 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
2. **Reopen all general-regime terms** at playbook starting points: 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24 months.
3. **Separate title, capacity and fundamental warranties** into their own regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Require independent title evidence beyond DD-012.
4. **Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, expressly non-waivable.
5. **Replace the general disclosure** (DL 1.1–1.2; Sch 7) with specific fair disclosure. Reject deemed disclosure of the data room and public registers.
6. **Delete clause 8.3.** Any knowledge qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** require effective written consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
8. **Riverlark:** require a current payoff letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** add the AUD 420k and triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or require Seller funding.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to cover IP transfer, title and cure costs. Require proof of payment or a confirmatory assignment.
11. **Privacy incident:** require log preservation, an investigation timetable and regular updates. Make no assumption about breach, harm, notification or quantum. Refer the notification question to privacy counsel.
12. **Sandbar renewals:** request contracts and terms and assess. No automatic debt or price treatment.
13. **Tax and IP:** keep as separate open categories. Do not fold into the general regime.
14. **Mossvale and office lease:** obtain counsel's view on whether the share sale triggers consent or notice.
15. **Bring-down:** require updated disclosure and data room confirmation as at signing and Completion, not 22 September 2026.

*This analysis applies the playbook as provided. Privacy (NDB scheme), tax (payroll tax, super, withholding) and contract consent questions should be confirmed by the relevant specialists before we take positions on them.*
=== END ADVICE ===
